[飞书用户 曹晓玉 (ou_533f5b3d594a23d3fe94ba4e0a7a33b1)]: 你觉得当前最新版论文的引言写的好吗，引言行文思路如下：
第一段（Hook）：用一个具体场景开门——"用 GPT-4 标注仇恨言论，做完标准混淆矩阵校正后，分析结论说政策对年轻用户增加了仇恨言论，但真实效应是保护性的。" 然后一句钉死："This sign reversal is not an edge case." 用因果结论被翻转的戏剧性吸引注意力。
第二段（背景 + 标准做法）：铺 LLM 作为标注工具在社科中的普及（成本低几个数量级），然后描述当前公认的校正流程：取一批专家标注 → 估混淆矩阵 → 统一反矩阵校正 CATE。读者读完觉得"这个流程合理"。
第三段（转折：问题在哪）：紧接着打破上面的安全感——LLM 标注误差不是均匀的，Ashwin et al. 发现跨人群误差率差 5 倍，我们的 pilot 里 GPT-4.1 误差从 10.2% 到 20.0%。这就为核心论点制造了前提条件。
第四段（核心发现）：当误差率跨子群异质时，标准校正不但不帮忙，反而更糟。给数字：14.9% 的配置下 CATE 符号被翻转（τ=+0.03→τ̂=−0.059），τ(0)=0.01 时升到 31%。所有 8 个真实 LLM 都放大偏差，而 EC-HTE 消除了符号翻转。一句话点明机制：过度校正——全局校正按平均误差率校准，在低误差子群里引入了本不存在的偏差。
第五段（理论贡献 + 文献定位）：给出精确偏差恒等式（Theorem 1，R²≥0.97），7.4 倍偏差缩减。然后一口气列出所有现有方法（PPI、DSL、PPCI、ForestIV）并指出它们的共同盲点：假设预测误差同质，无一处理 effect modifier 的子群异质错分类。完成文献 gap 的定位。
最后（贡献列表）：三个 bullet 对应三层贡献：
1. 理论层：偏差恒等式 + 无需估 τ 的诊断准则（Proposition 5）
2. 实践层：操作指南（Δπ>0.15, n≥250, K≤4 时用子群校正）
3. 方法层：EC-HTE 具体实现（层次贝叶斯 + κ-guard），兼容三种因果估计器和 PPCI
整体叙事逻辑：场景冲击 → 标准做法看似可靠 → 揭示隐患 → 量化危害 → 理论解释 → 现有方法都没解决 → 我们的三层贡献。是经典的 "break then fix" 结构。

\begin{abstract}
Large language models increasingly replace human annotators in computational social science, yet their error rates can vary by up to $5\times$ across demographic and text-feature subgroups.
When these noisy labels serve as effect modifiers in heterogeneous treatment effect (HTE) analysis, the standard remedy, estimating a single confusion matrix and applying its inverse uniformly, is widely trusted to remove bias.
We prove it can do the opposite.
We derive an exact bias identity showing that global correction introduces a subgroup-level bias proportional to the interaction of error-rate deviation and effect heterogeneity, a product structure invisible to any pooled analysis.
This identity reveals that correction reverses estimated causal effect signs in 14.9\% of configurations and amplifies bias across all eight real LLMs tested.
A diagnostic corollary flags harmful correction from error rates alone, without estimating treatment effects.
Guided by the identity, we propose EC-HTE, a per-subgroup correction via hierarchical Bayesian confusion matrix estimation that reduces bias by $7.4\times$ under extreme heterogeneity, with clear operating conditions ($\Delta\pi > 0.15$, $n_{\text{expert}} \geq 250$, $K \leq 4$) and validated across 11 LLM--dataset combinations spanning four NLP tasks\footnote{Code and data: \url{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/ec_hte_llm_annotation-4CC8/}.}.
\end{abstract}

\section{Related Work}
\label{sec:related}

\subsection{Measurement Error in Causal Inference}

Classical measurement error theory shows that naive regression with mismeasured covariates yields attenuated coefficients~\cite{fuller1987measurement,carroll2006measurement}.
\citet{frazis2003estimating} derive exact bias formulas for OLS with a misclassified binary regressor, showing attenuation proportional to the error rate, but restricted to average effects without subgroup heterogeneity.
In the econometrics literature, \citet{black2000racial} demonstrate that racial misclassification in administrative data biases disparity estimates, and \citet{bound2001measurement} survey how binary misclassification attenuates regression coefficients.
Our Theorem~\ref{thm:bias_identity} generalizes the Frazis--Loewenstein scalar result to subgroup-heterogeneous error rates, revealing a qualitatively new product-form bias that can reverse effect signs across subgroups.

\subsection{Post-Prediction Causal Inference}

Several frameworks correct for machine-generated label noise in causal estimation.
PPI~\cite{angelopoulos2023ppi} and DSL~\cite{egami2023dsl} use a small expert-labeled sample to debias predictions, assuming homogeneous prediction quality across observations.
PPCI~\cite{sui2026ppci} extends this to outcome-side misclassification, and ForestIV~\cite{bu2023forestiv} uses forest-based instrumental variables.
\citet{audinet2025benchmarking} benchmark these methods, finding that debiasing can increase MSE when prediction error is heterogeneous, a population-level analogue of the subgroup-conditional bias amplification we formalize.
All assume a single global error model; none addresses per-subgroup effect modifier misclassification.

\subsection{Heterogeneous Treatment Effects}

Modern HTE estimators, including causal forests~\cite{wager2018causal}, DML~\cite{chernozhukov2018dml}, and recursive partitioning~\cite{athey2016recursive}, assume error-free covariates.
When the effect modifier $Z$ is an LLM annotation, error rates can vary by up to $5\times$ across demographic subgroups~\cite{ashwin2025bias}, violating this assumption.
\citet{imai2010causal} study treatment misclassification (errors in $T$, not $Z$), requiring instrumental variables; our setting preserves the treatment contrast but corrupts the heterogeneity structure, making confusion matrix inversion feasible.
Extended discussion appears in Appendix~\ref{app:related}.

1	\section{Experiments}
2	
3	\subsection{Setup}
4	
5	We test on synthetic ($N{=}5{,}000$, $K \in \{2, 4\}$, controlled $\Delta\tau$ and $\Delta\pi$, 100 Monte Carlo (MC) runs) and semi-synthetic data-generating processes (DGPs) spanning four NLP tasks: sentiment analysis (TweetEval~\cite{barbieri2020tweeteval}, $K{=}4$), hate speech detection (CivilComments, $K{=}4$), stance detection ($K{=}5$; Appendix~\ref{app:stance}), and topic classification (AG News, $K{=}4$; Appendix~\ref{app:agnews}), with full specifications in Appendix~\ref{app:dgp}.
6	
7	We compare: (1) \textit{Naive} (no correction), (2) \textit{Global} (pooled confusion matrix, equivalent to PPI/DSL~\cite{angelopoulos2023ppi,egami2023dsl} with homogeneous error), (3) \textit{Stratified MLE} (per-subgroup DSL without shrinkage), (4) \textit{HB EC-HTE} (per-subgroup correction), (5) \textit{PPCI}~\cite{sui2026ppci}, and (6) \textit{EC-HTE+PPCI}.
8	For CausalForest~\cite{wager2018causal}, we compare naive, global, and EC-HTE variants.
9	Primary metrics are $|\text{bias}|$, root mean squared error (RMSE), and 95\% confidence interval (CI) coverage, averaged across subgroups and 100 MC runs.
10	Robustness validations cover eight conditions including asymmetric errors, subgroup misspecification, and treatment-dependent misclassification (all $\geq$89.5\% coverage; Appendices~\ref{app:hatespeech}--\ref{app:treatment_dep}).
11	Semi-synthetic evaluation uses empirical confusion matrices from 11 LLM--dataset combinations (eight LLMs across two datasets; Appendix~\ref{app:realcm_bias}; semi-real CM validation in Appendix~\ref{app:semireal}; open-source LLM validation in Appendix~\ref{app:multilm_opensource}).
12	
13	\subsection{Empirical Validation of the Bias Identity}
14	\label{sec:bias_mechanism}
15	
16	\begin{table}[t]
17	\centering
18	\caption{Results under moderate heterogeneity and semi-synthetic data. Moderate: $\Delta\pi \leq 0.10$; TweetEval: empirical subgroup structure ($K{=}4$). Metrics averaged over subgroups, $z$-levels, 100 MC runs. $^\dagger$RMSE exceeds Global.}
19	\label{tab:main_supp}

22	\begin{tabular}{ll ccc}
23	\toprule
24	Configuration & Method & $|\text{Bias}|$ & RMSE & Cov. \\
25	\midrule

38	\end{tabular}}
39	\end{table}

41	We verify Theorem~\ref{thm:bias_identity} on a $K{=}2$ grid (520 configurations, $\Delta\pi \in [0, 0.25]$, $\Delta\tau \in (0, 0.50]$) and a $K{=}4$ grid (Appendix~\ref{app:dgp}).

47	\paragraph{Real-world case study.}

\section*{Limitations}
\label{sec:limitations}

Per-subgroup correction requires sufficient expert labels ($n_{\text{expert}} \geq 250$ for $K{=}2$, $\geq 500$ for $K{=}4$) and moderate classifier accuracy ($\text{FPR}_s, \text{FNR}_s < 0.5$); at $K{=}8$, RMSE exceeds global correction under fixed expert budget (Appendix~\ref{app:k8_subgroups}).
Assumption~(A3) requires balanced effect modifier prevalence; under class imbalance ($P(Z{=}1) = 0.1$), the identity remains exact ($R^2 \geq 0.976$) but EC-HTE's RMSE advantage narrows (ratio 1.06--1.68; Appendix~\ref{app:classimbalance}).
Assumption~(A1), conditional independence of misclassification and potential outcomes, is not empirically testable; sensitivity analysis shows robustness up to $\gamma_T \leq 0.05$ for treatment-dependent misclassification (coverage $\geq$89.7\%; Appendix~\ref{app:treatment_dep}).
Ground-truth subgroup CATEs are unavailable in public datasets because classic causal inference benchmarks lack the LLM annotation step that creates the measurement error we address, so all evaluations use synthetic CATE injection on real text features and real LLM annotations (Appendices~\ref{app:dgp},~\ref{app:multilm}).
When LLMs annotate both the effect modifier and the outcome variable, covariate-side and outcome-side misclassification errors may be correlated, violating the independence structure assumed by combining EC-HTE with post-prediction causal inference (PPCI) frameworks~\cite{sui2026ppci}; practitioners should verify error independence or apply joint correction when both variables are LLM-annotated.
